prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create a production texture atlas for close-up fictional vehicle cabin interior materials, with the realism of high-end first-person video game material scans. Flat orthographic ALBEDO ONLY, even cross-polarized illumination, no perspective, no environment, no objects, no directional shadows, no cartoon styling, no bloom. Exactly four equal square tiles in a 2x2 grid with no gutters. TOP LEFT: authentic worn dark olive-gray painted steel, subtle orange-peel paint grain, fine scratches, small abrasions exposing dull silver metal, scattered faint oil smears and grime, restrained realistic contrast, mostly intact matte paint. TOP RIGHT: photoreal worn black tactical glove leather and flexible dark rubber material, very fine pebbled grain, subtle shallow wrinkles, realistic scuffing, flat material swatch without any hand or object. BOTTOM LEFT: authentic muted olive-drab woven flight-suit fabric material, visible fine twill fibers, subtle mottled wear and small stitch-like weave lines, flat fabric swatch without clothing shape or objects. BOTTOM RIGHT: a 4x4 grid of sixteen small realistic rectangular maintenance decals and industrial placards, each black or faded ivory backing with restrained white technical lettering and tiny diagrams; include labels reading CAUTION, NO STEP, HYDRAULIC, BATTERY, SERVICE, FLIGHT SYSTEMS, INSPECT, and SECURE; several narrow worn yellow-and-black safety stripe labels and serial number plates. The decal tile remains entirely flat. Weathered practical materials, sophisticated realistic restrained color, no logos, no watermark. Source texture for actual Blender PBR surfaces, not a rendered cockpit illustration.
usage: Scanned-look paint, leather, fabric, and maintenance decals. Normal and roughness maps are generated in Blender; occlusion is baked into GLB vertex colors.
